scope: Supporting source checks; no additional frozen attribution hypotheses.

checks.title: Fr10370 text order, marks and previously documented placement
checks.summary: Image2 ends with candidate Ardore caritatis succensa quem; image3 begins sepultum noverat sublatum cred[ens?] de sepulchro. The concatenation matches candidate Cantus601029a, supporting2→3 relative text order. Visible margin marks and the earlier catalogue placement remain separately recorded. A fixed translation-only screen and a fixed SIFT/mutual-ratio/RANSAC screen then tested the declared 1/2 and 3/4 boundary ROIs against the 2/3 different-surface control.
checks.outcome: Intrinsic relative text order is supported. With the proposed1/2 same-surface association and one-leaf catalogue assertion, numeral-surface before k-surface is consistent with the Finnish medieval-side convention. No general MPO rule, physical stitch, new placement or catalogue error is established. Neither proposed boundary passed the predeclared feature-registration screen (1/2: 4 RANSAC inliers from 9 mutual matches; 3/4: 5 from 28; 2/3 control: 5 from 18).
limits: Photograph indices are not medieval page sides.
Complementary portions in images1/2 suggest continuation, but no pixel registration or shared complete row proves an overlap.
The MPO meaning of1r/1v has not been established; the side-pattern mismatch remains conditional.
The older placement and later suggested group assertion have different scope.

Quem is expanded from an abbreviation and credens is partly uncertain; the normalized reference must not silently replace the literal reading. Cantus text came from public search indexing of primary database records, not inspection of those comparator images.

Feature matching is a test for repeated photographed detail, not a test of adjacent-but-nonoverlapping page regions. Failed registration cannot prove different faces; low-inlier homographies are not joins.

checks.title: Repeated opening address: conditional consistency check
checks.summary: Indexed institutional descriptions assign hVIII–hIX to IV156f2 and IV157f5 with different feast labels. All16combinations of four explicit consistency premises were evaluated.
checks.outcome: Unresolved. Different feast labels alone do not demonstrate mutually incompatible text or different books.
limits: The source readings came from public indexed institutional text with OCR noise; corresponding manuscript images were not verified.
Unique unrepeated numbering, correct transcription, the same physical position and incompatible text must all be established.
Reset numbering, composite volumes, side labels and incomplete summaries remain alternatives.

New indexed IV157 boundary assertions and its proposed interleaving of temporal/sanctoral units caution against an assumed simple global numbering sequence. This is a catalogue interpretation, not verified quire structure.

checks.title: Published image-scaling formula: possible erratum
checks.summary: Duba2023 printedp64/PDF66 prose scales width by Smin/Sn; the displayed equation reverses this ratio. Dimensional derivation and three analytic controls preserve physical size with the prose ratio.
checks.outcome: Use width × Smin/Sn when rescaling to Smin pixels/mm. This is an implementation correction and possible typographical erratum.
limits: No claim of first notice, originality or new historical finding.
The checks use synthetic analytic examples, not measured manuscript data.
No specialist or author confirmation has been received.

checks.title: Fr20274 against actual C23 pages and the editorial apparatus
checks.summary: A declared ten-site comparison uses actual C23 attachments0144/0145, Fr20274 and Hallqvist PDF67. Eight target sites are evaluable at word/cue/structure level; two remain unavailable. Current readings, visible corrections and editorial reports of old states are recorded separately.
checks.outcome: Seven current/standard word or cue agreements and one written-scope difference; no distinctive shared uncorrected C23 error established. This does not establish copying direction, a unique transmission branch or physical identity.
limits: Sites were selected after prior target/page review; this is not blind validation or a corpus-frequency test.
Cancelled C23 wording is only partly legible; full old states are editorial assertions where specified.
The target lacks the end of the second antiphon; two informative sites are explicitly unevaluable.
A written hymn cue differs; no performance omission is inferred.
C435 original images were not inspected. No melodic or correcting-hand/date inference is made.
